reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation of assist quality fundamentally shifts from discrete, subjective counting statistics to continuous spatial-temporal analysis. Traditional metrics rely on arbitrary binary classifications—whether a pass qualifies as an assist—which introduces significant noise due to non-uniform human judgment. By leveraging optical tracking data, we construct a rigorous mathematical framework grounded in Euclidean geometry and kinematics. The core operator, path congestion, quantifies the difficulty of a pass by measuring the minimum Euclidean distance between the ball's trajectory and the positions of opposing defenders. This transforms the qualitative concept of 'vision' and 'tight windows' into a quantifiable scalar field. Furthermore, the introduction of a projected linear trajectory allows for the calculation of intersection probabilities with defender positions. The dualities emerge between the physical execution of the pass (speed, distance) and the cognitive execution (navigating congestion). Failure modes arise when the assumption of linear ball flight breaks down under extreme arc conditions, or when the point-mass approximation of defenders fails to account for reach and lateral movement speed. Ultimately, these operators provide a robust, multi-dimensional vector representing the true value created by a passer, independent of the resulting shot's success.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling the passer requires inferring their predictive capability regarding receiver positioning and defender movements. The passer acts as an optimization agent seeking to maximize path clearance while minimizing transit time. Conversely, defenders act as stochastic obstacles attempting to minimize this clearance. The metric captures the passer's ability to anticipate and exploit transient gaps in the defensive manifold, effectively quantifying their cognitive mapping of the court.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent collinearity, path congestion must be strictly orthogonalized against pass distance and speed. A long pass naturally encounters more defenders; thus, raw intersection counts are insufficient. Leakage occurs if the model conflates the quality of the pass with the shooting efficiency of the receiver. A veto condition is applied if the receiver's historical shooting percentage heavily skews the perceived value of the assist, ensuring the primitive isolates the passer's contribution alone.
